newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Germany plans more cash for Vulkan's eastern yards.
newsitem.headline: Germany plans more cash for Vulkan's eastern yards.

text.p: The German authorities have asked the EU if they can give Bremer Vulkan's two former eastern shipyards almost one billion marks, European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Wednesday.
But the Commission was unlikely to approve the new aid to the yards unless Bonn submitted a plan on the misuse by Vulkan of German subsidies and how it intends to correct the situation, he said.

The plan would also have to include capacity cuts in return for the new aid to the MTW-Schiffswerft and Volkswerft yards and the cuts would have to be made in Bremen, the western city-state where Vulkan's main operations are based.
"The whole thing only has a chance of approval if capacity is reduced in Bremen," Van Miert told reporters.

Earlier on Wednesday the Commission said it suspected Vulkan had diverted 788 million marks approved for its two eastern yards -- 200 million marks more than assumed when the Commission started its investigation in February this year.
EU industry ministers would be asked to take a final decision, Van Miert said.

"I can't tell my colleagues this (new aid) is to compensate (the eastern yards for the money diverted) that's why I need to go to the Council (of ministers)," he said, indicating the affair was too sensitive to be decided without the ministers' backing.
The Danish shipbuilding association, backed by the Danish government, filed a complaint with the European Court of First Instance against the payment of subsidies to the German sector.
The court rejected the complaint last month, but the Bremer Vulkan case has raised fears all over Europe that German subsidies are out of control.
